findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user can receive a notification email for a topic without an existing topic_users row, e.g. after record cleanup, or simply never having visited). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, producing a 500 for anyone clicking the unsubscribe link in an email. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or handle the nil case.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking callers that don't supply it
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` interpolate it for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` (plugins, other mailers, and any email not going through `send_notification_email`) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send. A default/fallback or a separate key is needed.

findings.title: State-changing action exposed over GET without CSRF protection
findings.body: `unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level but is registered as a GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) and `check_xhr` is skipped. Mail clients, link scanners, image/link prefetchers, and any third-party page embedding `` can silently mute topics for logged-in users. The unsubscribe should either require a POST/PUT confirmation or be gated by a signed one-time key (like the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow).

findings.title: 301 permanent redirect used for a mutating endpoint
findings.body: The slug-less `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route redirects with `status: 301`. Browsers and intermediaries cache 301s permanently, so if the topic title (and therefore slug) later changes, clients will keep hitting the stale cached URL. Use 302 here, especially since the target performs a state change.

findings.title: Email text promises unsubscribe but action only downgrades to regular
findings.body: The new server locale text says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here", but the controller only lowers watching/tracking to `regular` on the first click and requires a second visit to mute. A user clicking once will still receive notifications (e.g. for replies to their posts), contradicting the email and the client-side message "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>".

findings.title: New unsubscribe route may be shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
findings.body: `topic` resource declares child route `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost` under `/t/:slug/:id`, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` can be matched as a topic with nearPost="unsubscribe" depending on route definition order/dynamic-segment matching. Declaring the more specific `topicUnsubscribe` route after the `topic` resource risks the unsubscribe page never rendering (and a bogus post-stream request for post "unsubscribe").

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe controller action
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action contains non-trivial branching (slug redirect, level toggle, missing TopicUser) and is reachable by any logged-in user via a GET link in emails, yet no request/controller spec was added. Regressions such as the nil TopicUser crash or wrong notification level transitions would go undetected.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i') in both the controller and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs. It works but is an API typo that will confuse future maintenance and theme overrides; rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.
